## Seat review — ⭐ **ACCEPT.** Reviewed at source on the branch, ⛔ not on the report.

`domain:ui` PM seat, `session_01UzHd6hDYatoDn17BuwKxnZ`. Merge-base `d8b4739` via `git merge-base` (⛔ not `base.sha` — lane fact 44). No contract-review record is owed: `Clause-②: no` was declared up front and the diff confirms it — three Tailwind utilities, one e2e spec, one changeset, and **no declaration of any kind**.

## The two things I said I would check first, both verified

**1. The fence — class strings only, no DOM restructuring.** Confirmed by reading the diff, not the report:

```
PageHeader.tsx     min-w-0  ->  min-w-48                        (unconditional)
DetailView.tsx     row:        + sm:flex-wrap
                   title col:  min-w-0  + sm:min-w-64
```

Three class strings. The element tree is untouched in both files.

**2. The pin asserts geometry, not classes.** `READABLE_H1_FLOOR = 192`, asserted against `h1.getBoundingClientRect().width`, plus clipping (`scrollWidth > ceil(width)`), tail containment and document overflow. The file carries its own note at the assertion — *"Not `toHaveClass('sm:min-w-48')` — a floor that does nothing would pass"* — which is exactly the acceptance bar the dispatch set.

⭐ And the extraction that feeds it is genuinely defended: the class strings are read out of the two sources at run time and compiled with the installed Tailwind, each walk **anchored and validated against a token that is not the floor under test**, so drifting onto a neighbouring element throws instead of silently measuring the wrong box. The report says that guard fired for real during development and is why `innerColumn` is ordinal 5 — a guard with a scar is worth more than one without.

## What earns the accept beyond the checklist

⭐ **The per-header divergence is reasoned, not fudged.** The dispatch said "report, don't stop, if the two headers want different floors" and the answer is better than the question:

- **DetailView** needs `sm:min-w-64`, one step above the precedent's `sm:min-w-48`, because *this* title column carries the 40px back button and its 12px gap **inside** it — so 256px is what leaves the h1 the same ~192px the precedent established. The before reading proves the arithmetic: `58.17 = 40 + 12 + 6.17`, i.e. the h1 rendered as an ellipsis and nothing else.
- **PageHeader**'s floor is **unconditional rather than `sm:`-scoped**, and the reason is the one that matters: the squeeze measures **worse just below `sm`** (639px: h1 10.59px of a 212px scrollWidth). ⭐ A faithful copy of the precedent would have left the worst reading in the file untouched. That is the kind of thing a class-shape test can never surface.

**The numbers are worse than the card guessed**, which is the right direction for a statically-identified card: 6.17px against the 29.5px objectui#7244 measured on the sibling.

**The one claim a reader would doubt was measured.** Replacing `min-w-0` with `min-w-48` could in principle restore the flex `auto` min-content minimum and blow the row out. It does not — an explicit `min-width` overrides that minimum exactly as `0` does — and rather than assert it, the dev measured a 92-character title at 799px: h1 751px of a 1682px scrollWidth, row still 799px, document overflow 0.

**The fixture sizing is honest about being a fixture, and about why it matters.** Sizing the tail to the app's real measured widths is load-bearing: a 786px DetailView tail exceeds the 799px row, the row's wrap drops it unaided, and the spec then passes **with the floor deleted**. Writing that reasoning into the file is the difference between a pin and a decoration.

**The void ablation is reported as void.** A mis-written guard skipped a restore, the next leg ran doubly-mutated and died as a wait timeout rather than a geometry assertion — reported, both redone from a clean tree, and the settle-wait changed because a `TimeoutError` hides the very reading a collapsed floor produces. ⛔ That is not a run to quietly repeat; naming it is what makes the clean table believable.

Each ablation reds **exactly one** test and leaves the roomy-viewport guard green, so the pin isolates the floor rather than the fixture.

## Out-of-scope handling — correct on both

- **objectui#9119** filed and ⛔ not fixed: the same header sizes its title column to the full title text below `sm`, pushing the page sideways (375px: title column 1201.22px inside a 375px row, 826px of horizontal overflow). ⭐ Measured **twice — on `d8b4739` and with this branch applied, identical to the pixel** — which is what establishes it as pre-existing rather than caused here. That is the right way to file a neighbouring bug found mid-change.
- The class-shape-only sibling test on objectui#7244's surface: noted, not touched, correctly outside this card's fences.

## Landing

`mergeable_state` was **behind** (base moved to `2c878be` when objectui#9115 landed). Merging the base in per lane fact 57 — ⛔ not re-running anything — then flipping to ready and arming auto-merge. Verified by queue ref, ⛔ never by the echo, which is currently returning a populated-but-wrong `method`.

⚠️ This PR says `Fixes #7281`, which is correct here — unlike objectui#9110 and objectui#9115, this card's scope is wholly discharged, so auto-close is right. The card's `pm:dispatched` and assignee will still need stripping by hand; `Fixes` has never done either in this lane, 35 times running.
